title: Canonical Gate repair index and range read authority
decisions: Reuse Context/Selection/Bundle/ContextRequest and existing publication/receipt/ledger paths.
Index manifest v2 commits every canonical page route, descriptor bounds and page digest; Bundle v2 remains the existing shared-table contract.

ContextRequest v1 preserves canonical range IDs. Optional intent inspect requests read-only inspection; omitted intent returns full repair. Redundant intent repair and host source selectors remain rejected.
Immutable snapshot query is pure and never reads or discovers checkout sources. Additional reads never grant writable targets.
Canonical source byte assertions apply to repair and inspection through the same source-storage boundary.
The generic source-effect exactKeys uses a different Error contract; repair exact-field validation is shared within the existing selection module to preserve TypeError contracts.

requirements.outcome: Revision-bound complete canonical inventory and page identity
Read-only locate/navigation/inspection refuse operations, foreign units, stale identities and duplicates
Saved inquiries reconstruct exact findings, sources, pages and target digests; full repair restores canonical evidence, all pending units and original allowedTargets
Captured-source query cursors bind source, complete unit identity, revision and parameters; exact union byte coverage controls progress
Inspection byte/provenance readback rejects tampered evidence against the immutable snapshot
No new checkout source ability or additional edit authority
